problem: The new copy-and-sweep rule (linked worktrees left out, submodules/embedded clones copied, own mutate-scratch never copied 'also with --scratch tmp', sweep thresholds 'two minutes' / 'ten minutes' / 'six hours') is restated by hand in five places: docs/docs/guides/review-with-a-record.md:197-202, docs/docs/cli-reference.md:5107 (mutate row), src/commands/review.ts:5087-5093 (help text), and both mirrored SKILL.detail.md files (:791-795). impact: The next person who tunes a threshold must find and edit every copy; this very diff shows the cost already paid — it has to repair review-with-a-record.md:1140, where one copy of the gate paragraph said 'two in a row' while the other copy and MAX_REVIEW_GATE_STALLS said three.

problem: The same fake scan — `const controller = new AbortController(); const reviewGateState = async () => { controller.abort(); return openReview(); };` — is pasted into three new tests (lines 167-171, 178-182, 190-194). The diff already extracted `openReview()` for the return value but not the abort-then-resolve scan that is the actual shared fixture.
impact: Whoever changes how the abort is simulated (e.g. aborting before vs after the resolve) must edit three copies and keep them in step; a helper such as `abortingScan()` returning `{ controller, reviewGateState }` would make the three tests differ only in what they assert.

problem: Magic number: `0o170000` is the POSIX S_IFMT file-type mask, written as a bare octal literal with no name. Node exposes it as `fs.constants.S_IFMT`, and the sibling module src/review/mutate.ts in the same diff already imports `constants` from node:fs.
impact: A reader has to know the stat mode layout to understand what the `special:` signature encodes; a named constant documents the intent and removes the guess.

problem: Naming: `stalled` holds a sentence fragment of the stop report (' and no change in the first … entries …' / ' and no new artifact in the last …'), but reads as a boolean state (and sits next to the numeric `stalls`). It is then used inside `stalls >= MAX_REVIEW_GATE_STALLS ? stalled : ""`, which reads as 'if stalled, then stalled'.
impact: A reader of decideReviewGate has to trace the ternary to learn `stalled` is text; a name like `stallReason` says what it is.

problem: The parenthetical added to the treeHash exclusion list — 'ignored files (the scratch copy still includes them, except linked worktrees, which it leaves out)' — attaches the linked-worktree rule to the ignored-files item, implying linked worktrees are a subset of ignored files. They are a copy rule unrelated to ignoredness, and the same paragraph restates the linked-worktree rule properly four lines later (:791). The same text is in the bundled mirror src/gdskills/bundled/skills/review/review-orchestrator/SKILL.detail.md:788; cli-reference.md:5107 keeps the plain 'ignored files' wording, so the two documents now describe the treeHash list differently.
impact: An agent reading the orchestrator detail may conclude that only ignored linked worktrees are left out, or that treeHash and the copy share one exclusion list.
quote: ignored files (the scratch copy still includes them, except linked worktrees, which it leaves out)

problem: SIGNATURE_WALKS_PER_STOP = 2 is now the divisor of MAX_SIGNATURE_FILES, but nothing ties it to the code it describes: findReviewGateState still hand-writes its two dirSignature calls. Adding a third walk would not change the constant, so the 'budgets together stay within MAX_HASHED_FILES' invariant in its doc comment (line 38) would silently break; only the TP-006 test checks the arithmetic, not the walk count.
impact: Observation only: settled if the walks were driven from a list whose length is the constant, or if the comment named the two call sites it must be kept in step with.
